newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro stocks hit records on dollar, Wall St.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro stocks hit records on dollar, Wall St.

text.p: Leading European stock markets surged to record highs on Friday with British investors relieved by stable interest rates and Germany buoyed by a strong dollar which had pushed the mark to its lowest level in years.
London and Frankfurt both broke through key index levels to record intraday highs, boosted by a 30-month high on the dollar and another record close on Wall Street.
Paris shares also hit new highs after a mixed start.
In London, the FTSE 100 stock index burst through 4,200 points to a record intraday high of 4,218. At late morning, the key index was up 7.2 points at 4,204.7.

"We look to be in an arena of low inflation and low interest rates," said one dealer. "Even though there's a little political uncertainty round the corner, the market will continue to reflect Wall Street, which is a raging bull at the moment."

News that underlying British inflation had slowed to 3.1 percent last month from 3.3 percent and finance minister Kenneth Clarke's decision to leave base rates at 6.0 percent for the time being underpinned market sentiment.
But the main impetus came from Wall Street despite efforts by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan to cool things.
The Dow Jones Industrial index shook off inflation jitters overnight to finish 38 points higher at a record 6,762 after being down 50 points at its worst.
"How solidly based it all is on Wall Street I'm not sure, but clearly the line of least resistance is upwards at the moment," one trader said.

"Wall Street is a huge bull, we have had several people trying to trip it up, including Mr Greenspan, but it has roared on again and still seems to have lots of momentum. We are on its tail," he added.
Not to be outdone by its larger European rival, the Frankfurt bourse also climbed into uncharted territory as the German DAX index broke through the magic 3,000 mark.
The DAX slipped slightly from early highs to hover around the 3,000 level. By early afternoon it was at 2,999.23, up 5.92.

Wall Street was also the main impetus here. Helping exporters, the mark has also fallen to its lowest levels in years due to a lacklustre German economy, talk of Bundesbank rate cuts and the drive towards European convergence.
The dollar hit a 30-month high of 1.6040 marks in early trading, up from its late Thursday level of 1.5952/62.

By early afternoon the dollar held just below the high as the market awaited U.S. trade data due at 1330 GMT and industrial output at 1500 GMT. If trade data for November shows the trade deficit is much bigger than expected, this could dampen the dollar, analysts said.
But they saw little fundamental reason for dollar weakness.

"The dollar's come up a long way quite quickly, particularly against the mark, and I suspect we're due for a bit of profit-taking correction... But there isn't an awful lot standing in its way," said Robin Marshall, chief economist at Chase Investment Bank.
"The markets have got the view now that if they don't run into official resistance, they're just going to take it higher," Marshall said.
A Reuters poll of economists showed an average forecast of a $9.8 billion deficit for the U.S. November trade balance.
Data for U.S. December industrial production, forecast on average to rise 0.6 percent after a 0.9 percent increase in November, would also be closely watched, analysts said.

French shares likewise hit an all time high before losing some of the gains. Again the reasons were the dollar and Wall Street plus special factors such as the sale by luxury goods LVMH of a stake in British group Guinness Plc.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 12.45 points at 2,420.22 after hitting a historic high at 2,426.13.
CURRENCIES AT 1145 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 117 yen and 1.6043 marks, compared with 116.53 and 1.5945 late on Thursday.
Sterling firmed to 2.6847 marks from 2.6745 late on Thursday. The French franc eased to 3.3720 marks from 3.3748.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1145 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was 7.2 points higher at 4,204.7, the first time it has gone through 4,200.
Frankfurt's 30-share DAX index broke through 3,000 before slipping and was up 5.92 points at 2,999.23 by late morning.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 12.45 at 2,420.22, also above Thursday's record close of 2,407.77.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was at $354.30, up from Thursday's close of $353.35. Silver was slightly stronger at $4.76, up three cents from the previous London close.
